name: Family Reunification Residency Card (Kurdistan Region)

requirements.blocker_text: Kurdistan Regional Government e-services (khzmat.gov.krd): a family-reunification residency card is available where one spouse is Iraqi and resides in the Kurdistan Region with residency support, and the other is a foreign national. Required: the Iraqi spouse's National Identity Card, Information Card, and residency-support documentation; the foreign spouse's passport (6+ months validity) and two photos; and a marriage contract from an Iraqi court, or a foreign marriage contract authenticated by the Iraqi Embassy and Ministry of Foreign Affairs. The foreign spouse must pass medical testing for HIV, hepatitis B/C, malaria, and bilharzia. If the foreign spouse is outside Iraq, a pre-entry visa is required first, and the Iraqi spouse must verify the foreign spouse's identity through the Immigration Administration's legal department. Processing takes 2 days. Fees: 25,000 IQD annual residency fee plus 10,000 IQD administrative fee. The card is valid 1-3 years.
requirements.fix_path: Gather the Iraqi spouse's ID documents and the authenticated marriage contract, complete the foreign spouse's medical tests, and file with the Kurdistan Region immigration authority -- a pre-entry visa is needed first if the foreign spouse is still abroad.

evidence_required.document: Iraqi spouse's National Identity Card and Information Card
Marriage contract (Iraqi-court or authenticated foreign contract)
Medical test results (HIV, hepatitis B/C, malaria, bilharzia)
Passport valid 6+ months plus two photos

sources.title: Kurdistan Regional Government official e-services portal (khzmat) -- family-reunification residency card requirements, fees, processing time, validity

notes: NEW COUNTRY BUILD (Iraq). STATUS: PUBLISHED -- hard requirement sourced directly to the Kurdistan Regional Government's own official services portal, tier 1. GENUINE FINDING: this is a REGIONAL (Kurdistan Region), not federal, process -- federal Iraq's equivalent family-reunification mechanism for foreign spouses of Iraqi citizens was not independently confirmed with comparable specificity in this build (see iq_citizenship_by_marriage.json for the separate, federal, citizenship-track spousal naturalization process under Law No. 26 of 2006, which is a different mechanism from this residency card). citizenship_after_months set to 60, reflecting the reduced 5-year marriage-based naturalization track (see iq_citizenship_by_marriage.json), not an automatic conversion from this card specifically. The 2-day processing time is unusually fast compared to most other countries in this dataset. dual_citizenship_allowed set to true per Iraq's Ministry of Foreign Affairs (tier 1, cited fully in the citizenship files). family_can_work left null: not addressed by the source.
